name: W22 Morning Flow — Bodyweight Spine + Hip (All Days, Rotated Variety)
description:
Fifteen minutes, three parts: primer, work, then the deep stretch arc. Work comes before the stretches because warm muscle stretches further.

This week rotates roughly half the moves. Thread-the-needle returns to the primer, the work block picks up spiderman planks and glute bridges, and puppy pose and happy baby come back into the yoga arc after a long absence. The rehab cluster and the pushup greasing set never rotate.

The QL has been sore all week — the cross-leg lateral lean in the add-on is where that gets addressed. Give it the full time.

exercises.notes: Full range both directions, breathing with the movement. Slow — this is the first thing the spine does today.

45s each side. **Back in the rotation after a long absence.** Thoracic rotation from all fours — reach the arm under and through, let the shoulder settle toward the floor. Rotation from the mid-back, not the lower back.
Standing, hinged slightly forward. Tight fists, thumbs tucked, rotate the wrists internally and hold the tension.
**Greasing set — never to failure.** Leave 2-3 in the tank. Elbows ~45°, **pack down not up**. This is a daily habit, not a training set.
**New this week.** From a plank, drive the knee to the outside of the same-side elbow. Hips stay level — don't let them pike up or sag. Slow, controlled, one side at a time.
**Ribs DOWN, low back flat to the floor.** That contact is the whole exercise — if the back arches off the floor, shorten the reach.

**New this week.** Feet flat, drive through the heels, squeeze the glutes hard at the top and hold a beat. **Ribs down** — don't arch the lower back to get higher. Wakes the posterior chain before it's asked to work.

sets.name: Yoga Flow — Deep Stretch Arc (~7 min)

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Thoracic + hip flexor opener. Let the top leg cross and the chest stay down.
**Back in the rotation.** Hips stay stacked over the knees, chest melts toward the floor, arms long. Thoracic extension and lats — the counter to a week of pulling and pressing.
45s each side. Deep hip opener. Forearms down if the hip allows it; stay on the hands if not.
Bodyweight, slow. Sit into one hip with the other leg straight, heel down. Adductors + hip mobility. **Take note of how these feel** — they're an early read on how fresh the legs actually are.
Wide straddle, reach to each side and then centre. Adductors and hamstrings — hold each reach, don't bounce.
**Back in the rotation after a long absence.** On the back, knees to armpits, hold the outsides of the feet. Inner hips and lower back release — a soft, passive close to the arc.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)

exercises.notes: **PUSH DAY.** 45s each arm at MID elbow height.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Face down, arms in a Y, lift with the lower traps. Slow, small range, no neck.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Plank position, arms locked, only the blades move. Protract and retract.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Elbow pinned to the ribs, small controlled range. Light or no weight.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Back flat to the wall, arms slide up and down keeping contact. Where it stops touching is the range you actually have.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** Passive hang, shoulders relaxed. Decompression.
**REHAB ANCHOR — every day.** From a dead hang, pull the shoulders down without bending the arms.
**LEGS DAY / QL WEEK.** 30s each side. The QL has been sore all week — give this the full time regardless of which day it is.
**LEGS + KB DAY.** 45s each side.
**ANY DAY.** 30s each side.

sets.notes: The six rehab anchors run every day. Add the day-specific pieces on top based on what you're training.

tips: **Order matters: work before stretches.** Warm muscle stretches deeper — don't reorder this.
**Rotated in this week:** thread-the-needle, spiderman plank, glute bridge, puppy pose, happy baby.
**Rotated out this week:** low-lunge thoracic rotation, inchworm walkout, McGill crunch, couch stretch, frog stretch.
**Never rotates:** the six rehab anchors (prone Y, scapular push-up, side-lying ER, wall angel, dead hang, scapular pull) and the pushup greasing set.
**Push-ups leave 2-3 in reserve** — this is a greasing habit, never a training set.
**Cossacks are an early warning system.** If they feel tired here, the legs are tired before the gym session starts — worth knowing before you read anything into a lift later that day.
**QL gets extra attention this week** via the cross-leg lateral lean.
Not too hard, not too long — this precedes a training session, it doesn't replace one.
